extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and commenters searching Federal Register rulemaking and notices about "junk fees" (consumer advocates, regulated businesses, lawyers, regulators)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results listing for documents and notices concerning "junk fees," aggregating proposed/final rules, notices, reports, and requests for comment from agencies (FTC, CFPB, FCC, etc.). Useful for finding regulatory standards, rulemaking questions, and supervisory findings about fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total price disclosure (clear, conspicuous, prominent)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an unfair and deceptive practice for businesses to offer, display, or advertise any price of live-event tickets or short-term lodging without clearly, conspicuously and prominently disclosing the total price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Trade Regulation Rule: require total price disclosure in advertising; businesses must include mandatory fees and charges so consumers see the full price up front. Applies to offers, displays, and advertisements; examples in the rule focus on live-event tickets and short-term lodging but conceptually applies to hiding mandatory fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-consent disclosure of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses must clearly and conspicuously make certain disclosures before a consumer consents to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade Regulation Rule requires that disclosures about fees be made prior to consumer consent to pay (not after purchase) so consumers can make informed decisions; applies to mandatory fees and charges and may include nature, amount, and refundability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresenting nature, purpose, amount, or refundability of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an unfair and deceptive practice to misrepresent any fee or charge in any offer, display, or advertisement, including misrepresenting the nature, purpose, amount, or refundability of fees or charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule language and rulemaking materials emphasize that misrepresentations about what a fee is for, how much it is, whether it is refundable, or other attributes are unlawful. Enforcement examples and comments (e.g., from consumer groups) illustrate harm when fees are mischaracterized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising that omits mandatory fees (bait-and-switch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bait-and-switch pricing that hides the total price by omitting mandatory fees and charges from advertised prices is an unfair or deceptive practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC Trade Regulation proposed/final rule identifies omission of mandatory fees from advertised prices as a core harm; agencies solicit comment and provide enforcement examples where advertised price excludes required fees, leading consumers to be misled about true cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposing fees without express informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposing fees or charges on consumers without their express, informed consent is an unfair or deceptive practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rental-housing rule and other notices highlight practices where fees are added without consumer consent (e.g., automatic enrollment or hidden add-ons). Comment solicitations request data on how often fees are imposed without express consent and examples of consent mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising rent that fails to include mandatory fees or charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising a rent price that does not include all mandatory fees or charges for rental housing is potentially unfair or deceptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC rental-housing rulemaking specifically cites advertising rent that fails to include mandatory fees (application, pet, parking, amenity, utilities-related, move-in, etc.) as potentially deceptive; solicitations ask for information across the lease lifecycle including application to move-out to assess prevalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees across the lease lifecycle should be evaluated (application through move-out)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess rental-housing fee practices, agencies seek information concerning fees and charges throughout a lease lifecycle—from application to move-out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC proposed rulemaking solicits written comment, data, and argument covering fees at all lease stages (application fee, move-in, monthly amenity/utility fees, move-out fees, repair/cleaning charges) to determine prevalence and need for rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and coverage of declined/NSF fees (including labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF/declined fees include fees charged after a declined transaction and labeled in many ways (e.g., returned item fees, returned payment fees, uncollected funds fees, overdraft—unpaid fees, returned payment fees). The proposed CFPB prohibition targets these fees for instantaneously declined transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB proposed rule on Fees for Instantaneously Declined Transactions defines the universe of covered fees broadly by substance (regardless of label) and intends to prohibit charges that would constitute abusive practices when a transaction is instantaneously declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on charging fees for instantaneously declined transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging fees (such as nonsufficient funds fees) when consumers initiate payment transactions that are instantaneously declined is proposed as abusive and should be prohibited for covered financial institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB frames such practice as abusive under the Consumer Financial Protection Act; rulemaking materials define scope (what counts as instantaneously declined) and list alternative labels that may be used for these fees to ensure the prohibition captures substance over label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees unauthorized by contract can be unfair; disclosed fees can also be unfair depending on circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Involuntary fees are often unfair when not authorized by a consumer contract, but fees that are disclosed in the contract can also be unfair depending on the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB Supervisory Highlights notes that authorization in contract does not automatically immunize a fee from being unfair; examiners assess context, practices, and whether the fee causes substantial injury or is deceptive or abusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcharging late fees (assessing in excess of permitted amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing late fees in excess of the amounts permitted (or inconsistent with contractual or statutory limits) is an unfair practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisory findings identify servicers charging late fees exceeding permitted amounts; agencies use examination and enforcement to address overcharging and require remediation where fees exceed allowed levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unnecessary or improper servicer fees (inspection, repossession, payment fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging unnecessary property inspection fees, estimated repossession fees, or abusive payment fees by mortgage servicers may constitute unfair or abusive practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB Supervisory Highlights and reports document exam findings where mortgage servicers charged unnecessary inspection or repossession-related fees or imposed unfair payment fees; these are evaluated under UDAAP (unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic practices that foreseeably cause multiple fees (re-presentment NSF fees) are injurious
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational system limitations that allow charging more than one NSF/re-presentment fee per item (or that cause cascades of fees) create foreseeable injury and may render the fees unfair or abusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB noted core processor platform limitations led to repeated NSF/re-presentment charges; examiners consider whether such systemic issues made the fees reasonably avoidable and whether institutions should fix systems or waive fees to avoid harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose existence and amount of all fees or charges of any type
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses should disclose the existence and amount of all fees or charges of any type (maintenance, monthly, connection, convenience, processing, upgrade/downgrade, service-specific, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC proposed trade regulation materials and enforcement orders emphasize comprehensive disclosure of all fee types and amounts; examples and settlement language require defendants to stop misrepresenting existence or amount of fees and to disclose them accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous labeling of fees and services (telecom/cable example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers (e.g., cable and internet) should list fees and services up front, on clear, easy-to-read labels so consumers can compare options and know bundled costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Consumer Protection Week and FCC rulemaking emphasize ‘clear, easy-to-read labels’ for fees and services (analogous to nutrition-label style disclosures) to reduce surprise or hidden fees for consumers selecting plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting/eliminating specific junk fees (early termination, billing cycle fees) for video services
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory proposals consider rules to protect consumers from video-service junk fees, including early termination fees and billing cycle fees (e.g., billing cycle alignment charges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC open-meeting notices describe NPRMs targeting early termination and billing cycle fees for video services; agencies seek comment on scope and mechanisms to prevent such fees from harming consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize discriminatory application of fees (fair lending concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposition of fees (including junk fees) that are applied more frequently or at higher amounts to protected classes (e.g., Black and Latino consumers) raises fair-lending and discrimination concerns and can lead to enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB and FTC fair lending reports and complaints allege that dealers or servicers charged extra or used fees in ways that disproportionately affected protected classes; agencies evaluate pattern-or-practice, consumer impact, and discrimination-based remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit data, examples, and arguments on prevalence and effects of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies routinely solicit written comment, data, and argument concerning the prevalence, scope, and consumer impact of fees (across sectors such as rental housing, mortgages, live events, short-term lodging, banking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of proposed rulemaking, requests for information (e.g., CFPB mortgage fees RFI, FTC rental housing NPRM) invite comments, empirical data, and stakeholder examples to inform rule design and scope; commenters are asked to provide lifecycle perspectives (application to move-out) and alternative policy solutions.
